stem: Mohan says, 'Lata's father is the only son of my father.' How is Mohan related to Lata?

per_option_rationale.rationale: The only son of Mohan's father is Mohan himself. Lata's father is Mohan. So Mohan is Lata's father.
Grandfather would require Mohan to be two generations above Lata. But Mohan is directly Lata's father (one generation above), not two.
Uncle would require Mohan to be a sibling of Lata's father. But Mohan IS Lata's father (the only son of Mohan's father = Mohan), so uncle is wrong.
Brother would place Mohan in Lata's own generation. The chain places Mohan one generation above Lata (as her father), not in the same generation.

explanation: The only son of Mohan's father is Mohan (self-reference). Lata's father is Mohan. So Mohan is Lata's father.

explanation_sections.punchline: 'Only son of my father' self-refers to Mohan, making him Lata's father.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: 'only son of my father' = Mohan (the speaker). Lata's father = Mohan => Mohan is Lata's father.
explanation_sections.lesson: When a chain resolves 'only son/daughter of my parent', it always resolves to the speaker unless stated otherwise.
explanation_sections.timing: About 40 seconds. The self-reference is the key insight. Trap is option 2 (grandfather) from over-counting generations.
